claim: Naively merging an instruction-tuned model into a reasoning model breaks the reasoning model's thinking-then-answer output format even though the two models' weight changes from their shared base are nearly orthogonal, so parameter-space orthogonality is not enough to make merging safe. Supported only if the principal subspaces of the two weight-change matrices have cosine similarity below 0.1 in every layer and module examined, yet plain task-arithmetic merging both shifts the output distribution at the thinking-delimiter tokens substantially and leaves more than 5% of instruction-following generations without a closing thinking tag, whereas a merge projected to leave the computation at those tokens unchanged cuts that distribution shift by more than tenfold and loses no closing tags.

experiments: Fix models, calibration data and benchmarks. Setup: reasoning models DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B/7B/14B/32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B; instruction-tuned models Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B/14B/32B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Merge only attention Q, K, V, O and FFN weights. Reasoning calibration set: 150 samples from Mixture-of-Thoughts (distilled from DeepSeek-R1); instruction calibration set: 365 DeepSeek-R1 responses to IFEval-style prompts filtered by an LLM judge and by hand. Instruction following on IFEval, CELLO, InfoBench and ComplexBench; reasoning and general ability on six math benchmarks (aggregated), GPQA, Aider code editing and Arena-Hard-v2 creative writing.

Measure how much the two models' weight changes overlap. Setup: for each layer and submodule, take the SVD of the reasoning and instruction models' weight changes from the shared base and compute the cosine similarity of their principal subspaces. Result: below 0.1 in every layer and module, suggesting little interference in parameter space.

Check whether merging preserves the thinking format. Setup: summed KL divergence of next-token distributions at the thinking-delimiter positions against the original reasoning model on held-out reasoning calibration data, and the share of IFEval generations missing the closing </think> tag, for task arithmetic and for the projected merge. Result: task arithmetic gives KL 0.1224 and 6.4% missing closing tags, which merges reasoning text into the constrained answer; the projected merge gives KL 0.0065 and 0.0% missing tags.
